_comment: UAE -> Switzerland email matchers. Built from a REAL confirmation email read out of mufaddal@travnook.com on 2026-09-24, minutes after the live registration that produced reference SWDB82370725773.
_comment_discriminator: SWITZERLAND BREAKS THE PATTERN THE OTHER THREE COUNTRIES SHARE. Greece, Italy and Netherlands are each narrowed by the portal URL in the body ('/are/en/grc/' and so on), which the AE-ITA config calls 'the only part of the message that names the country unambiguously'. That is not true here: the Swiss confirmation contains NO URL AT ALL. Its prose names the country instead — 'for a visa appointment from UAE to Switzerland' — so that phrase is the discriminator. Verified against the real message; re-check it if VFS rewords the mail.
_comment_why_it_mattered: Without this file the Swiss confirmation fell through every route's narrowed matcher (each demanding a URL the message does not contain) and was caught by the inherited 'vfs_other' catch-all — reported as unrecognised GREEK mail, with the reference left unextracted. Confirmed by classifying the real email on 2026-09-24.

matchers.name: waitlist_confirmation
matchers._comment: Overrides ONLY body_contains. subject_contains ('Successfully Added to Waitlist') and the extract patterns survive from _default, and both were verified against the real message: 'Dear MUFADDAL CALCUTTAWALA ,' yields the name even with the space before the comma, and 'Your Unique Reference Number is SWDB82370725773 .' yields the reference. SWDB is a FOUR-letter prefix where Greece and Italy use three; the base pattern [A-Z0-9-]+ already covers it.

matchers.name: waitlist_invitation
matchers._comment_validity: *** 12 HOURS. CONFIRMED from the real invitation read on 2026-09-24 — 'This link will only be valid for 12 hours'. *** This is the shortest window seen by a wide margin: Greece and Netherlands say 36, Italy says 48. Had this been left at the base's 48, a Swiss invitation arriving at 18:19 would have been shown as expiring in two days when it really expired at 06:19 the next morning — the client would have missed it while the system reported time in hand. That is exactly why this field was held null rather than guessed.
matchers._comment_body: CONFIRMED. The real invitation DOES carry the portal URL, unlike the confirmation email, so '/are/en/che/' would work here too. 'from UAE to Switzerland' is kept because it matches BOTH messages, and a single discriminator for the route is easier to reason about than two.
matchers._comment_sender: NOTE: the invitation comes from donotreply@vfsHELPLINE.com, while the confirmation comes from donotreply@vfsGLOBAL.com. Two different sending domains for the same route. The base matcher does not filter on sender, which is why both still match — do not add a from_contains here without checking both.

_comment_observed_confirmation: Subject: 'Successfully Added to Waitlist'. From: donotreply@vfsglobal.com. Body: 'VFS Appointment System Dear MUFADDAL CALCUTTAWALA , Your registration on the waitlist for a visa appointment from UAE to Switzerland under the General Appointment , has been successfully registered. Your Unique Reference Number is SWDB82370725773 . Your waitlist registration is active and is the only way to obtain an appointment for the General Appointment category. No further action is required from you at this stage. As soon as an appointment slot becomes available, you will automatically receive an email containing a link that will allow you to book your appointment.' — note there is NO link in this message, and the category reads 'General Appointment' rather than a visa type.
